en: Then the preceptor should worship Anantavijaya for the sake of the consecration;
for this [deity] is the source of all desired objects and the embodiment of the treasures. || 1 ||

First, in the northeastern direction of that [altar], upon a well-constructed auspicious seat (bhadrapīṭha) made of bricks, measuring two cubits [in length and width] and eight finger-breadths in height. || 2 ||
Above it was spread a canopy from which flower garlands hung down,
and it was adorned on all sides with many victory banners.
It was strewn with flowers, unbroken rice grains, and sesame seeds; it was delightful with the fragrance of incense and adorned with various leafy creepers and auspicious svastika symbols.
Upon a seat of darbha grass arranged on a prepared Śiva-pīṭha, one should consecrate the disciple stationed there with perfumes, flowers, and unbroken grains (akṣata). || 5 ||
With jars filled with water, adorned with garlands, cords, and cloths, marked with conch shells, svastikas, and lotuses, and well-smeared with sandalwood paste.
With water placed upon lotus petals, beautified by mango sprouts, and containing all kinds of gems, medicinal herbs, fragrances, kusha grass, and dūrvā shoots; (7)
With new and sturdy vessels made of gold, silver, copper, or clay,
placed in the directions starting from the east and filled with purified, auspicious water.
One should sprinkle [the disciple] with the eight root vidyās and the treasury of mantras, consecrated by Ananteśa and the other Lords of Vidyā (Vidyeśas) in the sequence as before.
Then one should greet him with the sounds of conchs and drums accompanied by lutes and flutes,
and with songs and shouts of victory.
Then, having led [the disciple] to the side of the mandala— either to the south or to the west—
he should cause him to stand upon a seat covered with a white cloth.
Having seated him in that office of authority, which has attained the status of a Mantra-pīṭha and is characterized by kusa grass, flowers, and unbroken grains (akṣata), one should worship him.

Having performed the ritual of sakalīkaraṇa according to the prescribed rule and having fashioned the "Hand of Śiva," the Guru [should worship it] with perfumes, flowers, purifiers (pavitra), and other offerings as available. || 13 ||
One should present to the preceptor the yoga-band, the rosary, a manuscript of the Saṃhitā, as well as a pair of scissors and a measuring cord.
Having thus worshipped him according to the rules while he stands in the position of authority,
the Guru should then cause the disciple to salute him from the status of a teacher.
Having caused him to enter the mandala, he should then address these words to the Lord of the Gods, who is seated and assumes the form of Dakṣiṇāmūrti: || 16 ||
One who stands in the state of grace should perform, day after day according to one's ability, the rites of worshiping Śiva, recitation, meditation, and fire-offerings. 17.
O Brahmin, you must indeed explain the meaning of the Tantra once, as it has been transmitted through the lineage of gurus, to those who are devoted to the knowledge of Śiva. 18.
To those who are pure, well-disciplined, whose minds are fixed on right conduct, and who have taken refuge in devotion to Śiva through their thoughts, words, and physical actions; 19.
Thus, favor should be shown toward those who possess such virtues, who desire liberation, and who follow the command of Śiva, without any deficiency in their constituent parts. 20.
This authority which has been transferred by me to you today must indeed be exercised by you until it has been transferred to another. (21)
Having bowed his head to the God and having received [the command] as it was spoken, he should say:
"May this auspicious glance of yours be upon us, so that we may proceed without obstacle. (22)
Then one should perform the fire-oblation (homa) according to the prescribed path;
having offered the full oblation (pūrṇāhuti) to Śiva, one should carry out the homa with the Brahma-mantras.

Therefore, the practitioner who follows the path must perform the fire sacrifice (homa) with three oblations using the limbs of Śiva, the limbs of Vidyā, the Lords of Vidyā (Vidyeśas), and the Root-Vidyā. 24.
Having attained this station, which consists of the sprouting of the festival of the Guru, the twice-born man should observe the vow of the teacher, the best of all vows. || 25 ||
The preceptor, who knows the rules for accomplishing feats, should perform the consecration of the practitioner—desirous of success—immediately after the mantra-homa. || 26 ||
Having worshipped the deity in the previously described maṇḍala exactly as before, one should then worship the mantra to be accomplished at the base of the śakti in every respect. || 27 ||
With fragrant flowers, perfumes, and scented waters,
with incense rich in fragrance, and with very white garlands.
With various pure offerings, well-prepared foods and edibles, with water for the guest-offering (arghya) endowed with its eight ingredients, and with lamps stationed in every direction; || 29 ||
Water, milk, kuśa grass, water from sacred scriptures, rice grains,
flowers, sesame seeds, along with barley and white mustard— this is declared to be the eightfold arghya offering.
One hundred and eight oblations, or half of that, or even a quarter, are to be understood as the number of offerings according to the specific mantras. || 31 ||
Ghee, milk, or sesame seeds soaked in ghee and honey;
bilva fruits smeared with ghee; and sacrificial fuel-sticks made from the Brahma-tree (palāśa). || 32 ||
A pill of Mahiṣākṣa guggulu, the size of an āmalaka fruit and smeared with clarified butter, is excellent; one should offer it as a burnt oblation for the sake of attaining success in the mantra. 33.

Then, according to the previously mentioned procedure, one should indeed consecrate the practitioner— who knows the meaning of the tantras and has conquered anger— seated upon the throne of the mantra to be accomplished.
Well-equipped with the ancillaries of knowledge, with his mind focused solely on the goal to be accomplished, perfected in purity and fasting, devoted to his guru, and firm in his vows. || 35 ||

With the waters from the previously mentioned jars, consecrated by the mantras of the sādhya, and with certain [substances] offered in the lustration ceremony (nīrājana) that have been drunk or likewise retained [within], [he should perform the rite]. || 36 ||
The Guru, standing on the south side of the image, faces north toward the image;
[toward] the north of the threefold image;
[toward] the north of the image.
The wise one, having performed the ritual of sakalīkaraṇa upon the practitioner, should worship him as before. || 37 ||
Then, having performed a circumambulation and entered the abode of his guru,
that best of teachers, together with his disciples, knelt upon the ground with both knees.
Having meditated upon Śiva and likewise the mantra, he should indeed place it in the joined palms of the practitioner,
pronouncing the mantra while using kuśa grass, water, sesame seeds, and unbroken grains (akṣata).
Then he should address the Lord: "O Śaṅkara, may there be success for him who has proceeded according to the scriptures without obstacle, by the will of Śiva. (40)
Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, on Consecration, in the Svāyambhuvasūtrasaṅgraha.
